The article mentions the Galaxy S26 Ultra will run Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip, which is a big deal for power and performance.

Also, the Galaxy S26 and S26+ might use the Exynos 2600 chip, but the Ultra’s all about that Snapdragon power.

Performance-wise, Snapdragon is seen as better for speed and heat, while Exynos is more efficient with battery.

Samsung’s likely launching the S26 Ultra in late Jan 2026 at their Galaxy Unpacked event.

Righto, the Galaxy S26 Ultra with Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 is a beast in raw power and efficiency, especially with AI processing improvements.

The latest iPhone (assuming the iPhone 17 Pro or whatever Apple drops around early 2026) will likely use Apple’s next-gen A-series chip, which usually nails performance and power efficiency, plus tight software-hardware integration.

Samsung’s got the edge on some hardware specs and possibly AI silicon support, but Apple’s iPhones tend to have smoother overall user experience and better software optimisation.

Righto, I see a solid breakdown here comparing the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra and the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro Max or iPhone 17 Pro Max, depending on Apple’s release cycle.

Samsung’s got:
- 6.9" Dynamic AMOLED 2X, 3000 nits brightness
- Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 or Exynos 2600
- 12-16GB RAM
- Cameras: 200MP main, 50MP ultrawide & telephotos
- 5000mAh battery, 45W wired charging
- Titanium frame, lighter, includes S Pen

Apple’s offering:
- A19 Pro (iPhone 17) or A20 chip (iPhone 18)
- Around 8GB RAM
- Advanced 48MP triple-lens camera
- Charging up to 35W wired, 50W wireless
- Possible under-display Face ID, new materials, foldable design option

Samsung leads in raw specs and camera hardware, Apple in chip performance and software polish.
